subject: Mathematics
source: OCR GCSE (9-1) Mathematics J560 specification (2015 onwards) — Y10 spec points across Number, Algebra, Ratio/Proportion, Geometry/Measures, Probability and Statistics. OCR uses content reference codes; this file uses subject-letter prefixed codes that match the OCR content tables.

specPoints.specTitle: Order positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions; use symbols =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥
Apply the four operations to integers, decimals and simple fractions including mixed numbers
Recognise and use relationships between operations, including inverse operations
Use the concepts and vocabulary of prime numbers, factors, multiples, common factors, common multiples, HCF, LCM and prime factorisation
Apply systematic listing strategies including counting principles (HT only)
Use positive integer powers and associated real roots; recognise powers of 2, 3, 4 and 5
Calculate exactly with fractions, surds and multiples of pi; simplify surd expressions involving squares (HT only for simplification of surds)
Calculate with and interpret numbers in standard form A x 10^n
Round numbers and measures to an appropriate degree of accuracy; use inequality notation to specify simple error intervals due to truncation or rounding
Apply and interpret limits of accuracy when rounding or truncating, including upper and lower bounds (HT for compound calculations)
Use and interpret algebraic notation, including ab as a × b, a^2 = a × a, coefficients written as fractions and brackets
Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions, including scientific formulae
Simplify and manipulate algebraic expressions by collecting like terms, multiplying a single term over a bracket, factorising into a single bracket and expanding products of two binomials
Factorise quadratic expressions of the form x^2 + bx + c, including the difference of two squares; factorise quadratic expressions of the form ax^2 + bx + c (HT only)
Simplify and manipulate algebraic fractions including factorising and cancelling (HT only)
Understand and use standard mathematical formulae; rearrange formulae to change the subject
Solve linear equations in one unknown algebraically; including those with the unknown on both sides of the equation
Solve quadratic equations algebraically by factorising; by completing the square (HT) and by using the quadratic formula (HT)
Solve two simultaneous linear equations in two variables algebraically; solve simultaneous equations where one is linear and one is quadratic (HT)
Generate terms of a sequence from a term-to-term or position-to-term rule; deduce expressions for the nth term of linear and quadratic sequences (HT for quadratic)
Plot and identify points on a coordinate grid in all four quadrants

Plot and interpret graphs of linear functions; identify gradient and y-intercept; find equations of straight lines through given points or parallel/perpendicular to a given line (HT for perpendicular)

Recognise, sketch and interpret graphs of quadratic, simple cubic, reciprocal y = a/x and exponential functions; recognise the shape of trigonometric functions y = sin x, y = cos x and y = tan x (HT for trigonometric)
Plot and interpret real-life graphs including distance-time and speed-time graphs; estimate gradients and areas under graphs (HT for non-linear gradients)
Use ratio notation; divide a given quantity into two or more parts in a given ratio; reduce ratios to simplest form
Solve problems involving direct proportion and inverse proportion, including using algebra (HT for inverse proportion expressed as y = k/x)
Solve problems involving percentages, percentage change, simple interest, compound interest, growth and decay; including reverse percentages
Calculate with compound measures: speed, density and rates of pay; convert between related compound units
Apply angle facts at a point, on a line, in triangles and in any polygon; deduce and use angle sums of polygons
Identify, describe and construct congruent and similar shapes by rotation, reflection, translation and enlargement (including fractional and negative scale factors — HT for negative)
Apply Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry in right-angled triangles; apply trigonometry in 2D and 3D shapes (HT for 3D)
Calculate perimeters of 2D shapes including parts of circles; calculate areas of triangles, parallelograms, trapezia, circles, sectors and composite shapes
Calculate surface areas and volumes of cuboids, prisms, cylinders, cones, spheres and pyramids
Use the basic vocabulary of probability; use the 0-1 probability scale; calculate experimental and theoretical probabilities
Calculate the probability of independent and mutually exclusive combined events using tree diagrams, Venn diagrams and two-way tables; calculate conditional probabilities (HT only)
Construct and interpret bar charts, pie charts, pictograms, frequency tables, line graphs and scatter graphs
Calculate and interpret mean, median, mode, modal class, range, quartiles and inter-quartile range; compare distributions
Construct and interpret histograms with equal and unequal class widths and cumulative frequency diagrams (HT for unequal class widths)
